== KIT LEVEL: THE COMPONENT CONTRACT — parts registry + states
  [PASS] registry: slider declares exactly (main, indicator, knob)
  [PASS] registry: bar declares exactly (main, indicator)
  [PASS] registry: bar IS slider minus the knob — one missing part is the whole difference between operating a value and being told one
  [PASS] registry: the state axis is LVGL's canonical six plus INVALID, in order — the seventh entry and the sixth CONTROL state, added by kits-learn-3 because a form screen had no seat in the contract and five languages invented the same red `!` to fill it
  [PASS] registry: a slider takes FOCUSED, EDITED and ACTIVE
  [PASS] registry: a bar takes NONE of them — no knob, no affordance of control, so no interactive state exists to be in
  [PASS] registry: CHECKED reaches the CHECKABLE components and nothing else — the REGISTRY says so, not a comment
  [PASS] registry: neither slider nor bar takes CHECKED — a value is not a boolean and the value family says so by not being CHECKABLE
  [PASS] registry: every component keeps DEFAULT and DISABLED
  [PASS] control: the state set is DERIVED from the parts — a NEW component with a knob gets the interactive states with nothing hand-listed anywhere
  [PASS] control: ... and a new component WITHOUT one gets none of them. A hand-written state table cannot do this, which is the reason there isn't one
  [PASS] registry: switch declares exactly (main, indicator, knob)
  [PASS] registry: switch declares the SAME parts as slider — the registry cannot tell them apart because on the axis it measures they ARE the same thing, and pretending otherwise would be a picture
  [PASS] registry: switch is CHECKABLE and slider and bar are not — one registry fact, and it is what makes them different components
  [PASS] registry: the switch's axis is the PRODUCT of its control block with the checked bit, not a hand list  ('default', 'focused', 'active', 'disabled', 'checked', 'checked+focused', 'checked+active', 'checked+disabled')
  [PASS] registry: every checked state of the switch is a base state with the bit set — the two halves of the axis are the same block twice
  [PASS] registry: a switch has NO EDITED state — EDITED means the arrows now RANGE through the value, and a boolean has no interior to range through; the press toggles at once, which is ACTIVE
  [PASS] registry: ... and the slider KEEPS it, so the removal is derived from CHECKABLE and not from the component's name
  [PASS] registry: the switch still takes FOCUSED and ACTIVE — it has a knob, and the knob is the affordance of control
  [PASS] registry: CHECKED|DISABLED and CHECKED|ACTIVE are FIRST-CLASS states, which is LVGL's own model and the reason the axis is a product rather than a sixth entry in a flat list
  [PASS] state algebra: control_of strips the checked bit
  [PASS] state algebra: with_checked SETS and CLEARS, and round-trips
  [PASS] state algebra: is_checked reads the bit and is not a substring match — `unchecked` would pass a substring test
  [PASS] state algebra: the glyph chain tries the combination, then the CONTROL bit, then checked, then default — a focused switch must look focused whether it is on or off
  [PASS] state algebra: every derived state resolves through the chain to a key the base table actually declares
  [PASS] registry: checked_pairs is DERIVED from the axis and covers it exactly once — the gallery's four rows are eight states
  [PASS] control: a NEW component declared CHECKABLE derives exactly the switch's axis — combinations included — with nothing hand-listed. A hand table cannot do this
  [PASS] control: declaring the SLIDER checkable takes its EDITED away and gives it the checked combinations — the derivation is reading CHECKABLE and not the component's name
  [PASS] control: ... and the registry is put back — a control that leaks state into the suite behind it is worse than no control
  [PASS] value model: the ends are the ends (4 cells)
  [PASS] value model: out-of-range CLAMPS — never wraps, never raises (4 cells)
  [PASS] value model: an INVERTED scale (min > max, LVGL's `_invert`) runs the other way with NO branch — the span goes negative and the fraction does the work (4 cells)
  [PASS] value model: position -> value -> position is EXACT in all four orientations (4 cells). The other direction quantizes, and a round-trip check claiming otherwise would be lying about what a cell can hold
  [PASS] value model: monotone UP on a normal scale and DOWN on an inverted one, across the whole domain (4 cells)
  [PASS] value model: the ends are the ends (7 cells)
  [PASS] value model: out-of-range CLAMPS — never wraps, never raises (7 cells)
  [PASS] value model: an INVERTED scale (min > max, LVGL's `_invert`) runs the other way with NO branch — the span goes negative and the fraction does the work (7 cells)
  [PASS] value model: position -> value -> position is EXACT in all four orientations (7 cells). The other direction quantizes, and a round-trip check claiming otherwise would be lying about what a cell can hold
  [PASS] value model: monotone UP on a normal scale and DOWN on an inverted one, across the whole domain (7 cells)
  [PASS] value model: the ends are the ends (12 cells)
  [PASS] value model: out-of-range CLAMPS — never wraps, never raises (12 cells)
  [PASS] value model: an INVERTED scale (min > max, LVGL's `_invert`) runs the other way with NO branch — the span goes negative and the fraction does the work (12 cells)
  [PASS] value model: position -> value -> position is EXACT in all four orientations (12 cells). The other direction quantizes, and a round-trip check claiming otherwise would be lying about what a cell can hold
  [PASS] value model: monotone UP on a normal scale and DOWN on an inverted one, across the whole domain (12 cells)
  [PASS] value model: a zero span never divides and never raises
  [PASS] one seat: `value_pos` is defined exactly once  1 definitions
  [PASS] one seat: so is `slider` — nine languages used to carry their own copy of the arithmetic, each with its own off-by-one (`w`, `w-1`, `w-2`, `w//3`), which is the fork defect the hero was cured of twice  1 definitions
  [PASS] one seat: and so are `readbar` and the composer they both call
  [PASS] one seat: the forked line is GONE — `span = max(1, hi - lo)` followed by a clamped round() was copied verbatim into every kit
  [PASS] one seat: ... and the law is not passing on a renamed string — the composer really does call the shared model

== KIT LEVEL: THE RADIO — can this contract hold a state whose SCOPE is larger than one component?

== KIT LEVEL: THE TEXT FIELD — the CARET enters the registry, and the value is CONTENT
  [PASS] registry: the text field declares `main` and `caret`, and CARET IS THE FIRST NEW PART THIS REGISTRY HAS TAKEN since it was written. It passes the bar the button's LABEL failed: the language draws it, from its own glyph table, and where it stands is state — none of which is true of the caller's words
  [PASS] registry: `caret` is genuinely new — no component that came before declares it, so this is a part entering rather than a name being reused
  [PASS] registry: AND IT IS NOT THE KNOB, which is the alternative that would have cost no new part. `(main, knob)` is the CHECKBOX's tuple; letting a field wear it would make one tuple mean two anatomies — a mark that is either there or not, and a mark at one of w places. Identical parts with different mechanisms is what this registry exists to make impossible
  [PASS] registry: no INDICATOR — a field measures nothing. Its interior is INDEXED, not measured, which is the distinction `has_interior` had to name
  [PASS] registry: it is NOT checkable — a field's value is neither a number nor a bit
  [PASS] registry: THE GRIPS are a declared registry fact, not a list hidden inside `actuator`. A knob rides a track and reports a magnitude; a caret rides characters and reports an index. Different parts, one thing to the hand — and a STEP is a third, which is the point of a declared tuple: it grew and `actuator` did not
  [PASS] registry: ... and every grip named there is a part some component actually declares — a grip nobody declares is dead metadata, which is the defect the button refused
  [PASS] registry: the ACTUATOR of a text field is its CARET, so the accent lands on the mark under the finger exactly as it lands on a slider's knob
  [PASS] registry: the axis is default / focused / EDITED / active / INVALID / disabled — six states, DERIVED, and the pair EDITED and INVALID is what this component was chosen to test: what the arrows can change, the form can reject  ('default', 'focused', 'edited', 'active', 'invalid', 'disabled')
  [PASS] registry: EDITED IS PRESENT AND IT MEANS WHAT IT SAYS HERE. On a slider it is 'the arrows now move the value'; here it is 'the keystrokes now land IN the text', and the caret is the promise of exactly that. FOCUSED is the field selected, EDITED is the field entered
  [PASS] registry: only the slider, the text field and the STEPPER take EDITED — the three components with a grip, an interior and no boolean. Every one of them arrived by derivation  {'stepper', 'slider', 'textfield'}
  [PASS] registry: `has_value` is FALSE — and that is the RULING, not an omission. The registry holds no value for a field because a field's value is CONTENT, which is what the button said about a label. It is also why no readout is printed beside it: the value is already visible IN the control
  [PASS] control: a NEW component declaring `(main, caret)` gets the text field's six states with nothing hand-listed — the derivation, not the text field, is what knows this
  [PASS] control: ... and its actuator is the caret, off GRIPS alone
  [PASS] control: a component with BOTH an extent and a field still gets six states — an interior counted twice is one interior, and the knobless grip is still the caret
  [PASS] control: declaring the field probe CHECKABLE takes EDITED away again — a boolean has no interior to range through, and that rule did not move when the caret arrived
  [PASS] control: ... and the registry is put back
  [PASS] control: TAKE THE CARET AWAY and the field collapses into a button — four states, no EDITED, `main` as its own grip. The caret is carrying the whole difference
  [PASS] control: ... registry restored again

== KIT LEVEL: THE SCROLL BAR — the value that is a WINDOW, and the SECOND SEAT beside `value_pos`
  [PASS] registry: the scroll bar declares the BAR'S EXACT TUPLE and adds NO new part. The caret was a new part because a state cannot pick out one cell; a thumb is not, because a scroll bar has no cell a bar does not have — a track and a run on it
  [PASS] registry: ... so every part it names was already declared — this increment grew the registry's FACTS and not its anatomy
  [PASS] registry: and THAT COLLISION is the proof the difference must be DECLARED. Two components share a tuple and differ in what their value IS — the registry has met this twice (switch/slider, radio/checkbox) and answered with a fact both times
  [PASS] registry: `VIEWED` is CHECKABLE's family, not a third kind of thing — CHECKABLE says the value's RANGE is boolean, VIEWED says its ARITY is two. Both are facts about a VALUE that parts cannot show; GRIPS is the one fact about parts
  [PASS] registry: NO GRIP OF ITS OWN — the scroll bar declares not one of the parts `GRIPS` names, which is the answer to 'a third declared fact is a smell': its pass added a fact and took none of the seats a grip would have moved. (The tuple has grown SINCE, at the stepper, and this component was untouched by that too)
  [PASS] registry: and CHECKABLE did not move either — a window is not a bit and does not join the product axis
  [PASS] registry: THE SCROLL BAR IS A READOUT — `actuator` is None. In this keyboard TUI the keys scroll the CONTAINER and the bar reports where the container got to; nothing here is ever grabbed, so there is no grip and the derivation says so without being told
  [PASS] registry: ... so its axis is DEFAULT and DISABLED and nothing else, and it is the BAR'S axis byte for byte. A FOCUSED scroll bar would advertise an affordance this app does not have — the same defect the bar's missing knob was the first cure for  ('default', 'disabled')
  [PASS] registry: ... and that is a CONSEQUENCE, not a preference — no control state is reachable, because the control block is gated on the actuator and there is none
  [PASS] registry: it HOLDS a value (an extent is declared) — which is why it is a readout and not a button: there is something to report, and no way to set it here
  [PASS] registry: it HAS an interior and still gets no EDITED — the interior term alone would have granted one, and the ACTUATOR gate is what refuses it. Two terms, and this component is the first to separate them
  [PASS] registry: the state axis is unchanged for every OTHER component — a new fact that moved an old component's axis would be a refactor wearing an increment's clothes

== KIT LEVEL: the COMPONENT CONTRACT — the STEPPER (wrap vs clamp)
  [PASS] registry: the stepper declares `(main, step)` — a word between two steps. It is the first tuple in this registry that is not a track, a box or a field, and the one new PART is what makes it one
  [PASS] registry: and NO NEW DECLARED FACT — `CHECKABLE` and `VIEWED` are byte-identical to what the scroll bar left them. The fifty-fourth pass warned that a third family would be a smell; this component answered by growing the ANATOMY instead, which is what the parts registry is for
  [PASS] registry: `GRIPS` grew instead, and that is the CHEAP kind of growth — a step is pressed, so it is the part under the finger, and `actuator` did not gain a term to learn that
  [PASS] registry: THE PARTS DIFFER FROM THE RADIO'S, which is why this is two entries and not one. A radio ITEM is a well and a mark drawn N times; a stepper is two affordances whatever the set's size — the same choice cannot be one anatomy
  [PASS] registry: ... and no OTHER component's tuple is `(main, step)` — the collision this registry refuses is identical parts with different anatomies, and it has not made one here
  [PASS] registry: it HOLDS a value — the seat it is at is a number the registry can read, which a text field's content is not. That is the third term `has_value` took, and the pair it makes with `has_interior` is the whole content ruling: a caret indexes cells the CALLER fills, a step chooses among seats the registry counts
  [PASS] registry: EDITED IS THE STEPPER'S HOME, and it is derived and not granted — a grip AND an interior AND not a boolean. On a slider EDITED means the arrows now move the value; here the arrows ARE the component, so this is the state the axis was built for  ('default', 'focused', 'edited', 'active', 'invalid', 'disabled')
  [PASS] registry: ... and no OTHER component's axis moved — a new part that changed an old component's states would be a refactor wearing an increment's clothes
  [PASS] registry: THE COMPOSER'S OPTIONAL STATE ARGUMENTS ARE STILL TWO — `caret` and `size`, the ones that default to 'nobody said'. `wrap` defaults to False because it is a RANGE word standing beside `lo` and `hi`: whether the scale closes on itself, which says nothing about where the value is. That is the fifty-fourth pass's warning answered by a distinction rather than ignored  ['caret', 'size']
  [PASS] control: a NEW component declaring `(main, step)` gets the stepper's whole axis, its grip and its interior with zero edits at any seat — the fifth anatomy belongs to the REGISTRY, not to the stepper
  [PASS] control: ... and it draws GROUND at the floor it cannot step off, exactly as the stepper does. One tuple, one mechanism
  [PASS] control: take `step` OUT of GRIPS and the stepper stops being a control — no grip, a value, therefore a READOUT with two states. The affordance is the registry's claim, and this is what it is worth
  [PASS] control: GRIPS is restored
  [PASS] seat: CLAMPED, the ends have NO STEP OFF at n=1 — the floor cannot go back and the ceiling cannot go on. That is what a clamp IS, and it is `None` rather than a repeat of the seat you are already at, because 'nothing happened' and 'you moved to where you were' are different claims
  [PASS] seat: ... and every INTERIOR seat has both at n=1 — a clamp takes away exactly two steps and no others
  [PASS] seat: WRAPPING, EVERY seat has both at n=1 — a ring has no end, which is the whole difference and the only one
  [PASS] seat: ... and the ends JOIN at n=1: the ceiling steps on to the floor and the floor steps back to the ceiling
  [PASS] seat: a step of ZERO is the seat you are on, wrapped or not at n=1 — the identity, which is what makes 'no step' mean something
  [PASS] seat: a step LANDS INSIDE the set at n=1, from every seat, in both directions, both readings — a stepper that stepped out of its own set would be the out-of-range selection the group seat refuses
  [PASS] seat: WALKING the set one step at a time reaches every seat at n=1 and STOPS at the ceiling — the reachability claim, asked by walking rather than asserted
  [PASS] seat: ... and WRAPPING it returns to where it started after exactly n steps at n=1, never sooner — a ring with a short circuit would be a set with a repeat in it

  [PASS] seat: ... but a set with NO SEATS raises, exactly as a group with no items does. A stepper through nothing is not a stepper
  [PASS] seat: `step_index` TAKES NO DEFAULT for wrap, and the vacuity prover is what found that: it had one, no caller ever reached it (both composing seats state their reading), and a value nothing can observe is dead metadata.   [PASS] seat: `step_index` is the ONLY place wrap is decided — it names no component and no language, so a ring is a property of a caller's range and never of a control
